kind: Primary-document research; no product execution or implementation

sources.title: W3C Indexed Database API 3.0
sources.finding: Strict asks the browser to verify storage writes before successful commit. A request success event is distinct from transaction completion. Durability is a hint with a performance and power cost.

sources.title: MDN StorageManager.persist
sources.finding: Persistent bucket permission is a separate request that the browser can decline; it is not evidence of transaction completion.

applications: Preserve strict transaction completion before command dispatch; no silent relaxed-mode fallback or automatic resending.
Actual browser tests should observe durability and complete/abort behavior. Controlled event-port results do not prove browser or physical durability.
Measure pending draft writes and flush latency under slow storage before considering safe coalescing; preserve handoff, CAS and generation barriers.
A future persistence/capability UI can be planned under an existing plugin contribution; do not add automatic prompts, a new slot or scope in the current implementation.
notClaimed: No new claim, installation or service
